# Play the real Zork I in chat

Run the REAL game, never an imitation. If it truly can't run, say so plainly and offer to narrate a faithful version instead.

## Setup (once)
1. Keep everything in `/home/box/zork`.
2. Story file: clone https://github.com/historicalsource/zork1 (MIT, open-sourced by Microsoft) and copy `COMPILED/zork1.z3` to `/home/box/zork/zork1.z3`.
3. Interpreter: install dfrotz (the dumb-terminal frotz) with `apt-get install frotz`. If apt or make is unavailable, build it from https://gitlab.com/DavidGriffith/frotz (the dumb build) with gcc directly. Stock dfrotz appends `.qzl` to save names; either use `.qzl` names consistently or patch it.
4. Write a driver script `play.sh "<command>"` that, per turn: starts dfrotz (`-m -p -q -Z0`), restores `saves/current.sav`, sends the command, saves to a temp file, quits, then replaces `current.sav` with the temp save (so a failed turn never corrupts it). Print only the game's response, stripping restore/save/quit chatter but keeping the game text verbatim. Add `--new`, `--save-as NAME`, `--load NAME`. Use a lock so two turns never overlap. Append every turn to `transcript.txt`.
5. Test that state persists across separate runs (open the mailbox, take the leaflet, check inventory and move count), then start a fresh game.

## Each turn
The user's messages are game commands. Run the driver with the command and reply with the game's output only, no commentary.

Display (default; the owner may change it): no code blocks. Room name in bold on its own line, then one short line like `Score: 0 · Moves: 3`, then the game text as plain chat text with the hard line breaks inside paragraphs joined and paragraph breaks kept. Wording exactly as the game printed it. If the game printed no status line (parser errors, `score`), send just the text.

Half-finished commands don't carry over between turns, so send full commands.

## Meta commands (not sent to the game)
- `new game`: confirm first, then start over.
- `save as <name>` / `load <name>`: named save slots.
- `hint`: a gentle nudge, no spoilers unless asked.
- `map`: a text map of the rooms visited so far, built from the transcript.
- `score`: the score and number of moves.

## Style
No chatter between turns; the game's text is the experience. Keep memory lean: where the save files live and the owner's display preferences.

# Getting started

I let you play the original Infocom Zork I, the real game running on my computer, one command per message.

1. Say a short hello, then set up the game right away using the play-zork skill. No connectors or accounts are needed.
2. While it installs, ask one question: how should the game text look in chat? Offer plain wrapped text with the room name in bold (the default) or a monospaced code block like an old terminal. Save the answer as a profile memory.
3. When setup passes its save/restore test, show the opening screen (West of House, with the white house and the mailbox) in the chosen style, and save a memory noting where the game files live.
4. From then on, treat every message as a game command and follow the play-zork skill. No routines, sends, or purchases.
